faq.q: Why don't deep-sea fish get crushed?
faq.a: Pressure squashes air spaces, and many deep-sea fish have none, no gas-filled swim bladder or lungs. Their bodies are mostly water, which hardly compresses, and the pressure inside matches the pressure outside.
asks: Why doesn't pressure squash deep-sea animals?
Do deep-sea fish have swim bladders?

faq.q: Why does water not get squashed?
faq.a: Water molecules are already packed closely together, so even huge pressure squeezes water by only a few percent. Air, with lots of space between molecules, squashes easily.
asks: Why do submarines need thick walls?

faq.a: TMAO, or trimethylamine N-oxide, is a molecule that helps proteins keep their shape under high pressure. Deeper fish have more of it. It is also what gives fish their fishy smell.
asks: How do deep-sea fish proteins work?

faq.q: What is the deepest fish ever found?
faq.a: In 2022, a snailfish was filmed at about 8,336 metres in a trench near Japan, the deepest fish ever recorded. Scientists think fish cannot live much below about 8,200 to 8,400 metres.

faq.q: Why does a blobfish look blobby?
faq.a: In its home 600 to 1,200 metres down, a blobfish looks like a normal fish, its jelly-like body supported by the water pressure. Hauled up quickly, its body slumps and is damaged, giving the famous blobby look.
asks: What does a blobfish look like underwater?

facts: Pressure in the sea rises by about one atmosphere for every 10 metres of depth.
A snailfish filmed at about 8,336 metres in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench in 2022 is the deepest fish recorded.
